metadata.title: Improved bounds for universal convex covers of unit arcs
metadata.abstract: Moser's worm problem asks for a planar region of least area containing a congruent copy of every unit arc. We show that the infimum area $\alpha$ among convex universal covers satisfies $0.239\le\alpha\le0.24633\ldots$, reducing the gap between the previous refereed bounds by over $75\%$. For the lower bound, we choose four unit polygonal arcs and prove by finite subdivision that, however they are placed, their convex hull has area at least $0.239$. For the upper bound, we construct a quadrilateral of area $0.24633\ldots$ and prove cover universality by showing that its support inequalities force uncovered arcs to have length greater than one. The full proof is formalized in Lean 4 and verified by the Lean kernel. Code and certificates are available at this https URL .
metadata.comment: 22 pages, 9 figures. Lean 4 formalization, code, and certificates available at this https URL
